D-lean-artifact.summary:
Lens D: the formal artifact. Primary sources are Alpöge's remark.pdf, the Lean community joint statement, Sutherland's MIT verification page, and the files in leanprover-community/riemann-hypothesis. Third-party build reports are rated medium.

1. **Distribution and licence.** The proof is a source tarball in 14 parts at alpo.ge: 239,275,554 bytes, 175,187 .lean files, 17,374,215 lines. It was published without a licence. Community mirrors exist "for verification only".
2. **Versions.** Lean v4.33.1 and Mathlib commit 0df444a3. The Lake package is named "tree" and has Mathlib as its only dependency.
3. **Statement.** The headline is `theorem riemannHypothesis : RiemannHypothesis`, using Mathlib's own definition.
4. **Dirichlet GRH.** The same artifact also proves GRH for Dirichlet L-functions (all moduli N ≥ 1, all characters), in four further theorems. con-leche and con-ron compare runs and nanoda accepted them on Sutherland's page. This is primary evidence that Dirichlet GRH now has a machine-checked proof. The joint statement certifies RH only. Dedekind, Hecke and automorphic L-functions are not covered.
5. **Axioms.** Only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
6. **Joint statement (21 Nov).** Endorsed by the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative. It names comparator, con-leche --compare, Lean's kernel, con-ron and unnamed third-party checkers. It does not mention Claude, GRH or Clay.
7. **Lean kernel nuance.** The Lean kernel's acceptance is shown by per-module replays of all 175,187 modules. Sutherland's single-threaded full-export Lean kernel runs were still running at his last update (22 Nov 04:35 UTC).
8. **Build cost.** About 2 to 13.4 hours on 32 to 512 cores. 256 GB nodes ran out of memory, and the recommended spec is 32 cores, 128 GB RAM and 150 GB disk.
9. **Caches and exports.** An untrusted community .olean cache is about 4.94 GB to download and about 96 to 99 GB unpacked. Sutherland publishes the export: 7.7 GB compressed, 61.57 GB unpacked.
10. **How the proof was found.** The remark gives a timeline compiled by Claude, from 6 Oct to 16 Nov 2026. It gives no token counts, model name or compute.
11. **Human-readable proof.** None exists. Alpöge says an informal write-up ran past 250,000 pages and he will write the proof up properly.

Practical answers:
- **(a) Using the theorem downstream: yes on a 32 GB Linux box; inferred.** Use the community cache and raise vm.max_map_count. Loading Main takes about 18.5 to 20.3 GiB RSS and needs about 110 GB of disk.
- **(a) On Windows:** tested only through WSL2 with 24 GB RAM and 16 GB swap, so in practice a laptop with at least 32 GB; native Windows is untested. A 16 GB box is untested.
- **(b) Re-checking the full export on 16 to 32 GB: no published route.** The smallest reported peaks are about 50 GB for con-leche and 78 GB for nanoda. What does fit, inferred: a statement-side audit, hash cross-checks, or a multi-day per-module kernel replay.

Not checked: secondary coverage (Nature, DataCamp) mentions a separate human-written RH proof announced about the same time.

claims.statement:
How it was found (remark.pdf, 4 pp, 20 Nov 2026):
- Alpöge, working with Claude, claims RH and GRH and expects ERH with more time. Claude and he formalized the argument without assumptions.
- He set up the analogue of a toy setting; he says Claude outpaced him near the finish.
- Claude's suggested chain of theta lifts had length √X for von Mangoldt sums of length X (Stepanov-style multiplicity).
- A Claude-compiled timeline runs 6 Oct 2026 (Stepanov determinant) to 16 Nov 2026 (GRH); many final steps are dated 15 Nov.
claims.source_title: Alpöge, remark.pdf
claims.notes: No token count, model name, compute or agent workflow is stated, and none was found elsewhere. The breakthrough came 'late Sunday night', probably 15–16 Nov (inferred).

claims.statement: Human-readable proof: none published. Alpöge says a huge unreadable document is routine to produce: Claude's informal 'GRH book' ran past 250,000 pages. He chose to present only Lean and intends to write the proof up properly. A third-party outline read from the Lean source exists (hhh2210): windowed Landau reduction, a CM-field identity giving an x/m + m bound, theta-lift chains with m ≈ √x, and a squeeze on period-lattice slope via Chowla–Selberg.
claims.source_title: remark.pdf; hhh2210/riemann-lean-account
claims.notes: The third-party outline is explicitly not certified by the Lean check.

Combined export: 61,752,134,938 bytes. nanoda accepted it in 33 min 46 s on 64 threads; con-leche --verified accepted 1,472,825 declarations; lake comparator v4.36.0 passed.

A-explicit-bounds.summary: Lens A, explicit prime counting. Every RH_only item below is now unconditional, given the 20-21 Nov 2026 Lean proof. Sharpest RH-era constants for code: psi uses Lee-Nosal, |psi(x)-x| <= sqrt(x)·log x·(log x - log log x)/(8π) for x >= 101. theta uses the same bound for x >= 2657. pi uses Schoenfeld, |pi(x)-li(x)| < sqrt(x)·log x/(8π) for x >= 2657; I found no sharper published explicit RH bound for pi. Gaps use Carneiro-Milinovich-Soundararajan: a prime in [x, x+(22/25)·sqrt(x)·log x] for x >= 4. Their Theorem 5 is stated forwards; the (x-c·sqrt(x)·log x, x] form is Dudek's. I found no improvement of 22/25 up to Nov 2026. 2026 RH-conditional notes: Chamberland-Straub give primes between x^(2+δ) and (x+1)^(2+δ) for all real x >= 1 when δ >= 1/4, so cubes for every n. Visser (arXiv, not refereed) gives x^(1/2+1/40) intervals for x >= 3.5e90 and power intervals for M >= 2.29. Best unconditional closed forms: Fiori-Kadiri-Swidinsky 2023 for psi (9.22106, exponent 0.8476836) and for pi (9.2211, against Li from 2). Korobov-Vinogradov shape: Johnston-Yang 2023 (x >= 23) and the newer Fiori-Jaskari 2026 (x >= 21, constant 0.239, 0.1982767). At x = 1e100 the KV bounds do not win generally. Johnston-Yang's KV psi bound is about 14.8x there (useless). Fiori-Jaskari is about 5.5e-3·x, against about 8.4e-2·x for the FKS closed form (my arithmetic). The RH bound is about 2.06e53, a relative 2.1e-47. Weak points: the PDFs could not be rendered here, so these come from arXiv abstract and HTML pages and citing sources. Visser, Fiori-Jaskari, Chamberland-Straub and Johnston-Sorenson-Thomas-Webster were checked from abstracts only. Fiori-Jaskari cite an 'OpenAI Oct 2026' zero-free half-plane Re s > 7/8; I have not verified it, and RH implies it anyway. The Arias de Reyna-Toulisse Theorem 6.2 wording came from a secondary snippet. The Cully-Hugill cubes threshold exp(exp(32.892)) came from a citing paper. Ramaré-Saouter's RH constant 8/5 is from memory and not verified. Journal volume and page numbers marked 'from memory' should be checked. GRH and other L-functions were out of scope for this lens.

claims.statement: RH implies |θ(x) − x| < (1/(8π))·√x·(log x)^2 for all x ≥ 599.
claims.source_title: Schoenfeld, Sharper bounds for the Chebyshev functions θ(x) and ψ(x). II, Math. Comp. 30 (1976) 337–360
claims.notes: Thm 10/Cor 1; 599 confirmed in citing sources. Pre-proof, Büthe's partial-RH method (RH to 3·10^12) made it unconditional for 599 ≤ x ≤ 2.169·10^25 (secondary).

claims.statement: RH implies |ψ(x) − x| < (1/(8π))·√x·(log x)^2 for all x ≥ 73.2.
claims.source_title: Schoenfeld 1976, Math. Comp. 30
claims.notes: 73.2 confirmed by Lee–Nosal and other citing papers.

claims.statement: RH implies |π(x) − li(x)| < (1/(8π))·√x·log x for all x ≥ 2657 (li = principal value ∫_0^x dt/log t).
claims.source_title: Schoenfeld 1976, Cor. 1
claims.notes: No sharper published explicit RH bound for π−li found (Lee–Nosal give ψ, θ, Mertens only).

claims.statement: RH implies |ψ(x) − x| ≤ √x·log x·(log x − log log x)/(8π) for x ≥ 101; and |θ(x) − x| ≤ the same expression for x ≥ 2657.
claims.before: Same unconditional bounds as Schoenfeld rows (FKS 2023).

verdicts.evidence: The AMS page returned 403. Platt–Trudgian 2021 Cor. 1 (seen in a search snippet) cites Schoenfeld Thm 10: RH ⇒ |θ(x)−x| < √x log²x/(8π) for x ≥ 599, and makes it unconditional for 599 < x ≤ 2.169·10^25. The 'before' constants agree with FKS 2206.12557: A=121.0961, B=3/2, C=2, R=5.5666305, admissible for x ≥ 2 by their Cor. 14.
Lee–Nosal v4 intro: RH ⇒ |ψ(x)−x| ≤ √x(log x)²/(8π) for all x ≥ 73.2, credited jointly to Schoenfeld and Grenié–Molteni. The primary AMS page was blocked (403).
Arias de Reyna–Toulisse eq. (67): 'Schoenfeld has proved' under RH that |π(x)−li(x)| < √x log x/(8π), printed for x > 2657. FKS 2206.12557 confirms li−Li = li(2) ≈ 1.04516.

Abstract v4 (2 Oct 2025): the same bound √x log x(log x − log log x)/(8π) holds for ψ when x ≥ 101 and for ϑ when x ≥ 2657. Thm 1.1 (x ≥ 11): √x log x(log x/(8π) − (1/(2π) + 1.465/log x) log log x + 1.2325). The cited earlier forms (x ≥ 2; x ≥ 2.3·10^9) match. No journal ref is listed.

Cor. 1.3 (HTML v4) uses the constant 3/(8π). Ranges: Σ1/p (B = 0.26149…) for x ≥ 24.4; Σ log p/p (E = −1.33258…) for x ≥ 43.1; e^C log x ∏ for x ≥ 23.8; e^{−C}/log x ∏^{−1} for x ≥ 24.2. The paper writes C = 0.57721…, i.e. Euler's γ. The proof is analytic for x ≥ 10^19 and computational below.

Büthe abstract (Math. Comp. 87 (2018) 1991–2009): |ψ(t)−t| ≤ 0.94√t for 11 < t ≤ 10^19. The θ bound is not in the abstract. Lee–Nosal cite Büthe Thm 2: |ϑ(x)−x| ≤ 1.95√x for 1423 ≤ x ≤ 10^19, so the θ part is second-hand.
DGM §4: 'On the Riemann hypothesis, Cramér was the first to prove p_{n+1}−p_n ≪ √p_n log p_n'. No constant is given. The BHP exponent 1/2+1/40 = 0.525 matches Visser's paper.

Abstract: RH ⇒ a prime in (x − (4/π)√x log x, x] for all x ≥ 2, improving Ramaré–Saouter. The constant 4/π can be replaced by 1+ε for large x. More than √x primes lie in (x, x + c√x log x] for c = 3+ε and x large. arXiv lists no journal ref, so IJNT 11 (2015) 771–778 is unverified.

Thm 1.1 (v2, IJNT, doi 10.1142/S1793042116500858): RH, x ≥ 2, c = 1/2 + 2/log x gives a prime in (x ± c√x log x) and at least √x primes in (x ± (c+1)√x log x). The text gives c = 0.55 for all x ≥ 5 when one prime is needed. Cor. 4.1 (α = 1 + 2/log n + 1/log² n, n ≥ 2) is also confirmed. Appendix A gives c = 0.6102.

PDF v2, Thm 5: RH and x ≥ 4 ⇒ a prime in [x, x + (22/25)√x log x]; the proof assumes x ≥ 4·10^18. Cor. 4: limsup ≤ 1/C⁺(B) < 21/25. Thm 3: inf c ≤ (1+2α)/C⁺(B) < (21/25)(1+2α). Supporting facts: C⁺(36/11) > 25/21 (1.9), and 1 ≤ B ≤ 36/11 (1.12, via Iwaniec). The paper also states p_{n+1}−p_n ≤ (22/25)√p_n log p_n for all p_n > 3.

Abstract (v1, 26 Feb 2026, unrefereed): RH + CMS + the Sorenson–Webster computation ⇒ a prime between x^{2+δ} and (x+1)^{2+δ} for all real x ≥ 1 when δ ≥ 1/4, with an explicit x0(δ) for smaller δ > 0. Taking δ = 1 gives cubes for all n ≥ 1. Its exponent 2.25 is better than Visser's M ≥ 2.29.

HTML v1, Thm 1: interval [x, x+x^{1/2+1/40}], exact crossover x* = 3.482755638·10^90 against CMS 22/25. Thm 2 uses CMS for x > 4.9·10^27 and the Sorenson–Webster upper-Oppermann check (n ≤ 7·10^13) below that. The paper never says x is an integer. For real x Thm 2 is false: with m = 15.831 the interval [7.01, 10.004] contains no prime, and it also fails for 23 < x < 23.15. Thm 3 has a typo in its interval and is weaker than Chamberland–Straub.
verdicts.corrected_statement: RH ⇒ a prime in [x, x + x^{1/2+1/40}] for real x ≥ 3.5·10^90, and a prime in [y^M, (y+1)^M] for y ≥ 1, M ≥ 2.29. The m-claim (0 < m ≤ 15.831) holds only for integer x ≥ 1; my own check of small x suggests it holds there. It is false for real x (e.g. 7 < x < 7.8). Unrefereed.

verdicts.evidence: Thm 6.2 (JTNB 25 (2013) 521–555): 'The Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to' |p_n − li^{-1}(n)| < (1/π)√n(log n)^{5/2} for all n ≥ 11. The paper writes ali(n) for li^{-1}(n). It is a true equivalence, so the bound now holds unconditionally.
Lagarias (1.2) and Prop. 3.1: Robin's criterion, RH ⟺ σ(n) < e^γ n log log n for all n ≥ 5041. Robin 1984 itself was not reachable.

Lagarias (2.2), citing Robin Thm 2: for all n ≥ 3, σ(n) < e^γ n log log n + 0.6482·n/log log n. The sharp constant is 0.648214…, with equality at n = 12 (σ(12) = 28), so Lagarias's 0.6482 with '<' fails at n = 12. The claim's 0.6483 with '<' holds (my check: RHS ≈ 28.0011 at n = 12).

Problem E: for each n ≥ 1, σ(n) ≤ H_n + exp(H_n) log(H_n), with equality only for n = 1. Thm 1.1: Problem E ⟺ RH. The cases n ≤ 5040 were checked by computer. Published in Amer. Math. Monthly 109 (2002) 534–543.

Abstract v3 (17 May 2023): |ψ(x)−x| < 9.22106x(log x)^{3/2}exp(−0.8476836√log x) for x > 2, and < 4.47·10^{−15}x for log x ≥ 3000, improving Platt–Trudgian's 4.51·10^{−13}x. arXiv lists no journal ref. At x = 10^100 the bound is ≈ 0.083x.

PDF v2, Cor. 22: |π(x)−Li(x)| ≤ 9.2211x√(log x)exp(−0.84768363√log x) for x ≥ 2; the abstract rounds this to 0.8476. Eq. (4): ≤ 0.4298x/log x for x ≥ 2. Li = ∫_2^x dt/log t. The paper says it improves Platt–Trudgian Cor. 2 and Johnston–Yang Cor. 1.3.

Abstract: ψ bound 9.39 for x ≥ 2. In the PDF, Cor. 1.2 gives θ with A1 = A + 0.01 = 9.40 (B = 1.515, C = 0.8274). Cor. 1.3: |π(x)−li(x)| ≤ 9.59x(log x)^{0.515}exp(−0.8274√log x) for x ≥ 2. arXiv lists no journal ref, so JMAA 2023 is unverified.

Thm 1.4, for x ≥ 23: (1.7) ψ with 0.026 and (1.8) θ with 0.027, both with (log x)^{1.801}. (1.9) uses 0.028 and (log x)^{0.801}; its left side is consistent with the printed |π(x)−x| typo. All use exp(−0.1853(log x)^{3/5}(log log x)^{−1/5}). At x = 10^100 the ψ bound is ≈ 14.8x.
